rows.issue: Frame adequacy is assumed, not shown
rows.detail: The bays are scored as clamped caps (O5) only when the stiffener rigidity EI_e/(a D_skin) is at least 10, a flat-plate order of magnitude. Mixed modes with wavelengths between a and 2a are not modelled.

rows.issue: The frame-bay knockdown is a transfer, not a measurement

rows.to_close: One bay test: a 2.04 m sandwich triangle (or a subscale bay at matched lambda_p and gamma_s) on a stiff frame ring, pressure-loaded, with the shape measured.

rows.issue: The stiffened-dome record does not show a higher knockdown
rows.detail: IDH CR-124075A p.4.1.012 gives 0.425 for heavily stiffened domes from one 1964 aluminium dome (C 0.26, plasticity suspected). CR-62257's plastic geodesic caps reached 0.57-0.64 of classical, while monocoque caps in the same program reached 0.78-0.82. SP-8032 p24 gives stiffened domes the isotropic cap curve (0.14 at a complete sphere).
rows.to_close: Any stiffened-sphere test at a realistic scale; until then, 0.425 is a one-test handbook value.

rows.issue: The heavy threshold psi 28 is this seat's computation
rows.detail: psi (composite over skin bending) of the IDH test dome is computed from CR-62257's design values (t 0.0375, d 0.166, b 0.10 in, side 1.65 in). As-built values were not extracted.
rows.to_close: Read the as-built dimensions in CR-62257 Chapter V.

rows.issue: Stiffener one-sidedness
rows.detail: SP-8032 warns that inside and outside stiffening can give seriously different dome results. The two-group model carries the offset in bending only, not the prebuckling-rotation coupling.
rows.to_close: FE with eccentric stiffeners on both sides.

rows.issue: Transfer bending is a simply supported bound
rows.detail: Bays carry the lattice's pressure share to the lines by bending, taken as the centre moment of a simply supported equilateral triangle, (1+nu) q a_t^2/54. It adds 45 MPa face stress at the Be-frame bay point. Continuous bays would see less.
rows.to_close: Plate FE of a continuous bay over the frame.

rows.issue: Rib-skin separation is not driven in the membrane state, but peel is unmodelled
rows.detail: The bond carries 0.16-0.21 MPa compression at the lattice lines. Peel in post-buckling, at rib ends and splices, and under thermal cycling is not modelled. No test exists of bonded Be ribs or tubes on a Be/aluminium-honeycomb sandwich.
rows.to_close: A peel and post-buckling coupon of a rib or tube on the actual sandwich.

rows.issue: SiC on Be thermal mismatch
rows.detail: 11.3 ppm/C (SR-200) against 4.02 ppm/K (Hexoloy-SA). The 25.1 K climate swing is included (1.83e-4 strain). Every 100 K between a hot cure and service would lock in 7.3e-4 strain, of the order of the membrane strain (about 1e-3).
rows.to_close: A room-temperature-cure route, or the CTE-matched Be frame (C2b).

rows.issue: Thin-wall tubes at the edge of the grid
rows.detail: The frame-bay designs pick r/t 300 tubes (0.26-0.29 mm walls). Tube local buckling (026's coefficient 0.6 x SP-8007 gamma, FIX-B) fails there (0.65 SiC, 0.78 Be). Manufacturability is unknown.
rows.to_close: Tube supply and local-buckling tests at r/t 150-300.

rows.issue: Rib material
rows.detail: Tees are taken as SR-200 sheet (blade plus foot, bonded) at sheet values. A machined S-200F tee would have about 255 MPa compression (030 ledger), below the 354-377 MPa rib stress of the heavy rib designs.
rows.to_close: A rib route decision and coupons.

rows.issue: The core at the lattice lines
rows.detail: Crush and W-direction shear at the lines use a w_bond + 2h spread. Heavy rib designs fail core shear (0.65). Local core densification is not costed.
rows.to_close: Local insert design and mass.

rows.issue: Lattice joining is a projection
rows.detail: Ribs: a 25 mm foot under one AF 0.015 lb/ft2 line, plus 5% of rib mass for splices and nodes. Frame: a 30 mm AF land plus two 5 mm paste fillets, 026's 0.02 kg nodes, and 023's Ti sleeves (157.7 kg at 562.2 kN, 030 register R064) scaled by member force.
rows.to_close: A joint card for ribs or frames on the sandwich.

rows.issue: The seam screen decides feasibility
rows.detail: 028's 10 MPa mean shear on a 30:1 scarf (300.333 MPa face stress) keeps every stiffened version from SF 1. A 40:1 scarf would cap at 400 MPa for about +3 kg of film. It is not evaluated as a route, because 028b's routes are fixed.
rows.to_close: A seam card if stiffening is pursued.

rows.issue: Smeared lattice idealisation
rows.detail: Equal members in three directions (nu 1/3). The frequency-6 geodesic has length scatter (026's mean arc is 2.001 m) and 12 five-valent joints.
rows.to_close: Discrete model (026 geometry).

rows.issue: 026's frame knockdown does not transfer to a skin-dominated hull
rows.detail: 026's 0.70-0.79 of linear is computed for a frame with t_eq about 2.6 r_o = 320 mm, where 10 mm is 3% of t_eq. Here it enters only frame-dominated designs (psi >= 28), and none of them carries a skin within the lift: 026's members alone weigh 4,567 kg.
rows.to_close: Measure a subscale frame if a frame-dominated hull is ever in reach.

rows.issue: The core-shear correction in the bays is standard, not tested
rows.detail: The thin cores of the heavy rib designs cut the plate load by about 60% (N/(1+kD/S)).

items.claim: 037's shear-lag screen holds each face at the core's expansion (0.227 after the 250 F cure). That needs the core to carry 47 times the in-plane force at which its walls yield. CR-1457, Hexcel AGU 075b and NASA TM-4585 treat the core's in-plane stiffness and thermal force as negligible; on that premise the continuous core carries no mismatch shear and a free core edge reads 1.17 / 0.83.

items.claim: The free-edge shear uses this seat's homogenised model: K_biax from wall stretching (uniform cell 0.5 E rho*/rho_s; doubled ribbon walls 0.45), a linear shear profile over half the core depth, and a 16 mm transfer length, about 1.7 cells. document.title: Paper benchmark not reproduced
document.issue: The CAX8 paper linear result is 30.21717 MPa versus published 27.53 MPa. Full 3D refinement gives 34.34704, 30.80495 and 30.28896 MPa, approaching CAX8 within0.24%; nonaxisymmetric modes at this resolution do not remove the roughly10% discrepancy. Elastic Gaussian-dimple endpoints exceed the published nonlinear pressures by over2x. No calibrated transfer of knockdown is established. The paper uses continuum-shell faces and tie constraints; ours uses conforming solid elements. No isolated cause for the linear discrepancy is claimed. Figure4 and the brief specify42.8mm radius; the conclusion says41.8mm. We use42.8mm and retain the text ambiguity.

document.title: Crushable foam missing

document.title: Different defect construction

document.title: Only axisymmetric lead modes
document.issue: Lead model excludes nonaxisymmetric and cell-scale modes. With L in the meridian the weaker W is circumferential and can trigger excluded modes. L orientation results are not full3D hull capacity.

document.title: Honeycomb continuum completion
document.issue: Only normalE and transverseGL/GW are sourced. InplaneE=.01MPa,G=.005MPa and zero core Poisson couplings are explicit regularizations. Actual cells, cell-scale dimpling, defects, adhesive, seams and debonding are absent. Increasing inplaneE/G100-fold to1/.5MPa changes accepted W linear eigenpressures by about0.0001% for021 and0.003% for021b; this limited sensitivity does not source the properties.

document.title: Faces remain elastic
document.issue: Neither beryllium nor stainless faces yield in the model. Beryllium inheritednu=.33 is used for comparison, not a verified grade-specific value. Known strength-basis uncertainty of021 is not resolved by these stability runs. NASA CR194164 Table2 reports SR200 in-plane nu12=.0768 andnu21=.0752 for1.96mm sheet. Treating.0768 isotropically at the lead gauge is itself a transfer. Its strong-direction endpoint98.34692kPa leaves only3.02% over operating pressure. A declared.03 sensitivity for021 gives91.468265kPa, below operating pressure. At the baseline endpoints, outer-face maximum equivalent stresses are660.806/835.808MPa for021 W/L and1144.503/1303.532MPa for021b W/L. These are von Mises diagnostics, not a verified beryllium criterion. Face survival to these loads is not established.

document.title: Finite-strain elastic convention differs from Abaqus
document.issue: CalculiX2.21 manual6.8.1 identifies native *ELASTIC as linear PK2 stress versus Green-Lagrange strain (St.Venant-Kirchhoff). Abaqus linear elasticity instead relates logarithmic strain and Cauchy stress. Our decks specify no Ciarlet, hyperfoam or crushable-foam law. Large-compression behavior of this elastic approximation is not physical foam behavior. This adds a nonlinear constitutive mismatch; the separate roughly10% linear benchmark discrepancy remains unisolated.

The S-II inflation technique smoothed welded skins to fit the core; using an inflated inner skin as the mandrel is this card's proposal.
rows.to_close: Subscale assembly trial of either method.

rows.issue: Be dust limits where scarfs are cut
rows.detail: OSHA 1910.1024 sets a PEL of 0.2 ug/m3, so scarfing and trimming Be is regulated-area work (sub-worker row). JPL had all dust-producing Be operations done at the supplier. The route puts every Be cut before assembly.
rows.to_close: Supplier-side scarfing and handling plan.

rows.issue: Be face waviness at the wrinkle wavelength is unmeasured
rows.detail: The precedents are whole-panel RMS (reflectors 5-60 um; vendor honeycomb 0.2 mm) or cell depths. Treated as wrinkle-band amplitude, they map to Q 0.19-0.75 (this card). Wrinkle periods are near 37-40 mm (CHECK-032).
rows.to_close: Profilometry of a bonded Be/CR-III panel in the 20-60 mm band (F1, 038 T3).

rows.issue: Jig support spacing is this card's estimate
rows.detail: Self-weight is 34.2 Pa. A sandwich span sags 0.11 mm at 2 m and 4.2 mm at 5 m (simply supported strip), so supports belong 2 m apart or closer.
rows.to_close: Jig design with measured sag.

rows.issue: The first evacuation is the proof, and it is destructive
rows.detail: Sea-level evacuation loads the hull to 1.061 of its 500 m design pressure (038). A buckle at proof ends the hull, and no subscale proof precedes it.
rows.to_close: A subscale built shell evacuated first (T7).

rows.issue: Cost class is not scaled
rows.detail: Reflector-grade surfaces cost GBP 2-5M to refurbish or replace a 15 m dish (JCMT, 2011 talk) and about $5-6M per 10 m SMT (1987). Nothing here scales that to a 20 m sphere. Be stock is 020's $39.5-167.9M.
rows.to_close: Costed route after F1.

rows.issue: The route rests on 037b
rows.detail: The route adopts 037b's 200 F panel cure and 30.34:1 scarf. If CHECK-037b moves the stress-free temperature or the scarf rule, step 4 and the seam overlap change.
rows.to_close: Re-read step 4 against CHECK-037b when it files.

items.topic: Full-size ceramic material and contact reliability
items.finding: The best 5% closure witness requires 1.164235 GPa extreme compression under the declared amplified-demand screen. The 3.9 GPa typical compression value and fixed 15.586 MPa tension reliability projection are not qualified allowables for long, thin curved arcs or their contacts. The vendor sheet gives E=430 GPa; the dispatched comparison retains E=410 GPa.
items.needed: Production-representative arc and joint/contact tests, defect/size statistics, environmental durability, and a stated reliability model. Resolve the modulus edition and geometry transfer before claiming capacity.
items.prohibited_inference: No qualified compression allowable or assembly failure probability follows from the reported required stress.

items.finding: The matching-022d optimization retains its axial-stress local-wall formula. Substituting peak amplified compression into that formula lowers the selected frequency-5 witnesses from 1.143285/1.083205 to 1.033223/0.978132 at the 5%/019 reserves. This is a conservative sensitivity, not a calibrated interaction law.
items.needed: A verified local-shell model or tests for curved SiC tubes under combined axial force, end bending, contact and geometric imperfections. Reoptimize if the interaction changes the active local limit.
items.prohibited_inference: The 019 witness cannot be presented as robustly above unity across the displayed local-shell conventions.

items.topic: Joint strength, density, rotational stiffness and mass
items.finding: Actual member-end axial force, bending and torsion are included in the annular-sleeve and ring-bond demand. The selected frame reaches 3.356559 kN m end bending and 1.118657 kN m torsion. Equal-stress resized joints attain the requested scalar target by construction, without surplus reserve. The 1550 kg/m3 composite density is assumed; Toray's laminate strength and Henkel's prepared-aluminum shear result do not establish the proposed SiC joint.
items.needed: A joint architecture, laminate orientation/thickness, bondline and surface treatment, peel and transverse/torsional shear interaction, cyclic/environmental data, contact stress and measured rotational stiffness. Include all hardware mass.
items.prohibited_inference: Scalar sleeve/bond sizing does not establish a rigid joint, full multiaxial strength or a manufactured joint mass.

items.finding: A 270 GPa filament-derived axial tangent changes perfect linear multipliers, but the assumed taut, perfectly attached 0/90 skin has no qualified shear modulus, Poisson coupling, prestress, wrinkling, sagged equilibrium or free interior kinematics. The projected tangent can overstate restraint. No film-stiffness credit is used in primary resizing.
items.needed: An actual gas-tight laminate, biaxial and shear constitutive data, tension-only/wrinkling treatment, pressure-equilibrated geometry, seams and attachments, plus tear, creep, fatigue and permeability evidence.
items.prohibited_inference: Neither the fiber modulus nor the conditional pinned-film result proves a stable pressure vessel.

items.topic: Imperfections, nonlinear capacity and the global 0.2 factor
items.finding: The selected perfect f=4 frame has a verified first sampled elastic tangent loss near 5.430902; m12 to m24 changes it by about 0.35%. Smallest-algebraic values are checked along the sampled path and independently audited. The inherited 0.2 factor is not calibrated to this frame. Applying it to the nonlinear value would be an alternative arithmetic sensitivity near 1.086180. The primary resize retains 022d's 0.2-times-linear convention.
items.needed: Manufacturing and joint-imperfection distributions, path refinement as needed, measured stiffness, and validated nonlinear analyses for final resized candidates before adopting a capacity factor.
items.prohibited_inference: Perfect elastic first loss is not material/joint collapse, a global certification of every inter-step state, or a validated knockdown. The frozen 026b nonlinear paths remain unverified.

items.topic: Realized mass, volume and practical fabrication
items.finding: Actual integer counts add 178.319 kg of tube mass to the selected continuum point and leave 174.444 kg closure deficit at the 5% reserve. Resizing closes the declared arithmetic, but the cap sag and pressure-fan surfaces are distinct approximations. Film mass uses 4 pi R squared; node and systems allowances are inherited.
items.needed: Manufactured curved-tube tolerances and joints, gas-barrier/adhesive/seam/attachment mass, continuous or segmented arc feasibility, a pressure-equilibrated volume, assembly access, damage protection and a complete bill of materials.
items.prohibited_inference: Near-zero numerical closure residual does not establish physical vehicle mass closure.

items.topic: Beam idealization and initial bending coupling
items.finding: The linear eigenproblem uses segment compression geometric stiffness plus the conservative pressure Hessian; it omits initial-moment coupling. The separate corotational nonlinear selected-frame calculation includes the elastic tangent. Euler-Bernoulli circular beams do not resolve local shell ovalization, shear deformation, joints, contact or composite/ceramic defects.
items.needed: Cross-check with independently formulated beam/shell models and benchmark problems; resolve the relevant local and joint physics rather than treating mesh convergence alone as model validation.

items.finding: Frequency 5 ranks first at both reserves in the tested uniform-section family. Frequencies 1 through 10 were searched; 4/5/6 reoptimized at m6 and m12; 4/5 checked at m24. The final m24 witnesses keep the m12 gyration and solve exact mass closure. Multiple local starts and adaptive interpolation checks are not a global optimality certificate.
items.needed: Broader topology/nonuniform-section search and any necessary final exact optimizer refinement if a global optimum or minimum mass at the continuum target is required.
items.prohibited_inference: No claim of a globally lightest design attaining 022d's target is made; this card selected the brief's best-SF-at-closure option.

resolved_for_this_card_only.finding: The selected section is modeled directly; the transferred 026b ratio is not used. Its own perfect linear multiplier and explicit 0.2 screen replace that numerical shortcut, while material and model qualification remain open.

Smallest-algebraic eigenvalues at every recorded selected-frame equilibrium, independent shifted solves and finite-difference tangent checks establish the reported first sampled loss for the new m6/m12/m24 paths. This is not a retroactive claim about earlier cards.

inherited_037b.claim: 037's shear-lag screen holds each face at the core's expansion (0.227 after the 250 F cure). That needs the core to carry 47 times the in-plane force at which its walls yield. CR-1457, Hexcel AGU 075b and NASA TM-4585 treat the core's in-plane stiffness and thermal force as negligible; on that premise the continuous core carries no mismatch shear and a free core edge reads 1.17 / 0.83.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A curved Be/CR-III panel cured with AF 163-2U, cycled over 271-302 K, strain-gauged at a core splice, at a face scarf and in the field, then sectioned.

inherited_037b.claim: The free-edge shear uses this seat's homogenised model: K_biax from wall stretching (uniform cell 0.5 E rho*/rho_s; doubled ribbon walls 0.45), a linear shear profile over half the core depth, and a 16 mm transfer length, about 1.7 cells. Homogenisation is marginal there and cell-scale peaks are not modelled. The W direction governs over L on both strengths.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A cell-resolved finite-element model of a free core edge, or the panel test above.

inherited_037b.claim: The cure leaves the faces in compression balanced by core tension. This card takes it as not driving global buckling or crimping, because the wall's net membrane force is unchanged (this seat's argument). It adds it in full to yield, wrinkling, dimpling and the scarf; for wrinkling that is conservative, since the core's tension near the face resists the wrinkle.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A sandwich-shell buckling analysis with the layer-wise residual state.

inherited_037b.claim: 028b's fixed 30:1 scarf binds at its projected 10 MPa screen, so the cure compression costs usage (0.972 to 1.052); 028's sizing rule restores it at 30.44:1 for 0.16 kg. The 10 MPa screen is not a measured Be scarf allowable, and a filled core splice at the scarf may change the local face stress.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A measured Be scarf allowable and the splice-at-scarf detail.

inherited_037b.claim: 028b's faces are pinned by its fixed 30:1 scarf. Without any cure compression a 30.44:1 scarf would let them thin, to usage 0.894. 028b gives no reason for fixing 30:1, such as machining, overlap, peel or panel-edge limits. This card notes the lever and does not take it.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: 028b's owner states why the scarf is fixed at 30:1, or re-runs the least set with the scarf ratio free.

inherited_037b.claim: Whether 028's filled 0.5 mm core splice carries the core's in-plane force (no free edge) is not shown; the fill's modulus and its bond to the cut cell walls are unsourced.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Splice-fill properties and a splice coupon in in-plane tension.

inherited_037b.claim: The residual is a sustained shear on the core. On the minimum-average W strength (25 psi) it reads 0.83 at a free edge after the 250 F cure. Honeycomb creep and day-night fatigue under sustained shear are not sourced.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Sustained-load and cyclic shear data for CR-III 5056 3/8-1.0.

inherited_037b.claim: The cure-or-Tg rule (108-121 C for AF 163-2U) is sourced qualitatively; no measured stress-free temperature or relaxed fraction for AF 163 was found.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: A bimaterial-strip or panel-curvature measurement with the actual cure cycle.

inherited_037b.claim: Room-temperature pastes (EA 9394 class) carry no sourced honeycomb bond data, fillet mass or flatwise strength; they are priced at AF's areal weight.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Honeycomb flatwise and climbing-drum data for a room-temperature system at a weighed areal mass.

inherited_037b.claim: Hexcel prints only thickness-direction expansion for glass and aramid cores; their in-plane values are proxies here. The carbon core UCF-145 (12.8 kg/m3, second-hand shear data, W strength 97 kPa) has no sourced in-plane expansion or compressive modulus and is not priced.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: In-plane expansion and compressive data for candidate non-metallic cores.

inherited_037b.claim: NASA/SDSU co-cured-panel studies report the face/core cure mismatch as cell-wall distortion and face waviness. That is a source of the wrinkle coefficient's waviness (MAINLINE-032), not of bond shear.
inherited_037b.needed_to_ground: Measured face waviness after an AF 163-2U cure on CR-III.

Inserts, closeouts and 037's mooring pads constrain the mismatch locally; they are not scored here.

items.finding: The new coupled membrane/edge model balances pressure and thermal force but is homogenized over a short edge region. Pressure contraction may offset thermal residual extension; this is not validated relief.
items.evidence_needed: Cell-resolved and curved-panel validation of free edges, splices and hardpoints during thermal cycling, pressure hold and full vent/evacuation.

items.finding: 3M lap runouts and thicker supported-film failure curves do not qualify the actual 0.015 lb/ft2 U-film Be/core joint or the 200F cycle. Gross-area shear masks the sparse core-foot contact: a no-fillet area sensitivity gives 27.0 MPa at the 200F cold edge; effective fillet/contact area is not known.
items.evidence_needed: Actual-film, actual-substrate shear/peel/mixed-mode fatigue, process repeatability and environmental retention, with weighed fillets/primer.

items.finding: The face scarf uses HexBond312, a separate adhesive. Its 10 MPa screen is static and unsourced for this Be joint. No applicable S-N or crack-growth data were obtained.
items.evidence_needed: 30:1 and proposed 60:1 Be scarf fatigue and sustained-load tests including peel, roots, manufacturing flaws, leak integrity and repairs.

items.finding: HexBond312's cited cure is 120C. A later whole-panel scarf cure could invalidate an assumed 200F face/core stress-free state.
items.evidence_needed: An executable joining sequence and measured stress-free temperature/residual strain after every thermal operation.

items.finding: Adding the inherited local thermal envelope to 037b's cured point takes the scarf below its static screen. The extrema are conservative and not time-correlated.
items.evidence_needed: A complete combined-load, layer-resolved scarf/face/core solution and strain measurements at critical locations.

items.finding: The original pad area exceeds minimum core shear strength at its design load. The 950-day plate-only index excludes assembly support, cyclic plasticity, fasteners, backing and attachment notches.
items.evidence_needed: Detailed pad/insert load sharing and interaction solution, actual 6061-T6 properties/finish, local Be/core response and spectrum tests of the assembly.

items.finding: The resized pad uses a scalar p/2 reserve against core capacity and an extra allocation of the sum of plate/core Miner indices. Neither is a validated multiaxial failure law.
items.evidence_needed: A calibrated local core shear/compression interaction and separate statistically supported component life requirements.

items.finding: The quantified strict pad plus 60:1 scarf candidate adds 36.66 kg to an already balanced budget; lugs, fasteners, backing, monitoring and repair margins are additional unknowns.
items.evidence_needed: A complete installed bill of materials and a new floating equilibrium without silently consuming the fixed reserve or systems allocation.

items.finding: Gas-cycle amplitudes use assumed leak acceptance, permeability and 90% conditioning. Full venting can change release inventory; it is not equivalent to top-up.
items.evidence_needed: Whole-hull leak/outgassing tests and a defined vent/reconditioning/power service protocol.

items.finding: Room-temperature S-N screens do not supply ten-year humidity, salt, corrosion, UV/coating damage, creep, fretting or vacuum/environmental bond retention.
items.evidence_needed: Relevant environmental conditioning and fatigue/dwell testing with documented acceleration and retention factors.

items.finding: No defect detection threshold or crack/debond growth law supports an inspection interval. Plate replacement does not reset core, scarf or face damage.
items.evidence_needed: Qualified NDE probability of detection, initial-defect population, growth-to-critical size and tested repair procedures with a complete mass inventory.

items.finding: S-N damage does not quantify evolving waviness, debond-induced buckling, impact damage, or nonlinear aerodynamic/local bending stresses. Static projected gamma is not a life property.
items.evidence_needed: Cycled curved-panel and shell stability tests, validated imperfection growth and a combined-load nonlinear structural model.
